hook.text: A noisy phone line can carry only so many reliable bits per second. Shannon calculated that exact limit in 1948.

buildup.text: Channel capacity C is the maximum rate at which information can be sent with vanishing error probability.

discovery.text: Shannon proved: below capacity, reliable communication is possible. Above it, errors are unavoidable.

twist.text: He proved the limit exists but didn't show how to build codes that achieve it. That challenge lasted 50 years.

climax.text: Turbo codes in 1993 and LDPC codes finally reached within a whisper of Shannon's limit in real systems.

punchline.text: Shannon drew the line. Engineers spent decades reaching it.

quiz.question: What happens when you try to transmit above channel capacity?
options: Errors become unavoidable no matter the code
